key_insight: Coupling parametric finite elements with symplectic Runge–Kutta time integration yields high-order surface diffusion simulations that exactly preserve enclosed curve area without added constraints.
engineering_relevance: The method supports accurate simulation of area-conserving interface evolution, where numerical area drift can distort predicted shapes.
method: Discretize the classical BGN formulation using parametric finite elements.
Apply q-stage Gauss Runge–Kutta schemes with temporal order 2q.
Solve the fully implicit nonlinear system using an equivalent formulation and monolithic damped Newton iteration.
evidence_signal: Tests on various evolving curves confirm exact area preservation, high-order temporal convergence, and favorable mesh quality, with Newton iterations rapidly dropping below 8 per step.
watch_item: Unconditional area conservation does not by itself guarantee perimeter decay or robust nonlinear convergence for every time-step size.
paper_title: High-Order Area-Preserving Runge--Kutta Methods for Surface Diffusion Flow of Curves
